claim:mcdaniel-2019-sepsis.proposition: Sepsis progression by infection severity (McDaniel et al. 2019, Figs 4-7)
claim:mcdaniel-2019-sepsis.hypothesis: Peak pathogen and cytokine levels rise, and tissue integrity falls, from mild to moderate to severe infection. Only the severe arm decompensates: lactate exceeds 2 mM after about 20 h and SBP falls below 100 mmHg at about 26 h, as in the paper. Unlike the paper, MAP is not expected to reach 65 mmHg (septic shock) by 48 h on 8.2.0.

claim:mcdaniel-2019-treatment.proposition: Fluid challenge and antibiotic in severe sepsis (McDaniel et al. 2019, Figs 9-10)
claim:mcdaniel-2019-treatment.hypothesis: The challenge raises blood volume and pressure above the untreated arm within the hour it is given; the antibiotic's plasma level exceeds the pathogen's MIC (16 mg/L) and the blood pathogen falls below the challenge-only arm's by 52 h.

claim:mcdaniel-2019-refresh.proposition: REFRESH resuscitation protocols in severe sepsis (McDaniel et al. 2019, Figs 11-13)
claim:mcdaniel-2019-refresh.hypothesis: Both protocols raise SBP above 90 and MAP above 65 mmHg by the end of their 6 h; the experimental protocol does so with less saline than the control; the same control protocol started 12 h later meets a more hypotensive patient and gives more saline.

narrative.question: Does BioGears 8.2.0, driven through viva-biogears, reproduce McDaniel et al. (2019): sepsis progression by infection severity (Figs 4-7), the fluid challenge and antibiotic (Figs 9-10), and the REFRESH resuscitation protocols, on time and delayed (Figs 11-13)?
